overview: Black offers the f-pawn at once with 1...f5, hoping for ...Nf6 and ...e6/...d5 development and a Dutch-like game. After 2.exf5 White is a pawn up and Black has little for it; accurate development leaves White clearly better. It scores through surprise.

white_ideas.idea: Take on f5, develop quickly with Nf3, d4 and Nc3, and keep the extra pawn
Meet ...e5 or ...Nf6 with d4 and develop

black_ideas.idea: ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...d5 or ...e5 to get pieces out
Attack the white king if it opens the diagonal with Qh5+ or ...Qh4+

typical_structures.structure: White up a pawn with open e-file and f-file after 2.exf5

character.notes: Black takes risks at once and White punishes inaccuracy; open and tactical.

gambit.notes: 2.exf5 wins a pawn that White can keep.

structure.notes: Open e- and f-files after the exchange.

level.notes: Dubious line, never a first repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2.d4
sublines_that_differ.how: Declined, reaching Dutch-like set-ups; no material is given.

character.reason: Black gambits a pawn at move one; lines are forcing and open.

structure.reason: Open e- and f-files after exf5.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play it.

plans.reason: Black plays for quick development against the extra pawn.
